That's a retro transformation: It breaks a C-O bond (alcohol) to give a silyl ether? Actually forward: C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si]... -> [C:2]-[OH]. So retro: from alcohol to silyl ether? Wait retro direction is left to right? The retro_smarts_template is '[C:2]-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si](-C)(-C)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2]'. So applying to target (which has an OH) will give a silyl ether precursor plus maybe something else? Actually the product side is alcohol; reactant side is silyl ether. So retro: we replace OH with silyl ether group. So precursor will be silyl ether plus maybe something else? The template seems to generate a silyl ether attached to the carbon that had OH, plus a tert-butyl group? Actually C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si](-C)(-C)-O-... This seems to add a t-butyl-silyl group. Not realistic.
